clusters.headline_hint: US and Saudi Arabia conduct joint airstrikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq amid growing regional escalation

claims.text: US and Saudi Arabian forces launched coordinated airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilisation Forces bases in Iraq.
Iran-backed Popular Mobilisation Forces in Iraq allegedly carried out 30 drone strikes on Saudi Arabia prior to the joint US-Saudi counterstrikes.
De facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman initiated the Vision 2030 initiative to diversify Saudi Arabia away from dependence on oil revenues.
Satellite images on Monday showed that the Abqaiq oil facility in Saudi Arabia was struck by drones launched by Iranian proxy militias in Iraq.
On 13 July, Saudi Arabia bombed Sanaa airport outside the Yemeni capital to prevent an Iranian plane from landing, prompting Houthi retaliatory attacks on Saudi airports at Abha and Jizan.
Joint US and Saudi airstrikes on sites associated with Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces killed at least 20 fighters.
Iran launched missiles at US military installations in Jordan in its first attack in the region following a brief pause in fighting with the US.
On Wednesday, a drone strike hit a US-owned floating storage tanker at a natural gas loading port in Damietta, Egypt.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi cancelled a planned meeting with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah following the US-Saudi air raids.
US President Donald Trump stated that the United States would be "hitting [Iran] hard".
According to Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi, Egypt lost around $7 billion in 2024 due to decreased shipping traffic through the Suez Canal.
Revenues from the Suez Canal dropped from $10.25 billion in 2023 to around $4 billion in 2024 as annual transit ship counts halved from over 26,000 to just over 13,000.

clusters.headline_hint: Wildfires ravage parts of France, Spain, and Greece during severe summer heatwave

claims.text: Firefighters in France were placed on high alert as scorching temperatures and strong winds threatened to fuel a wildfire west of Bordeaux.
A wildfire west of Bordeaux burned about 420 square kilometers of France's Gironde region.
About 57,000 residents evacuated from three towns near the Gironde wildfire were allowed to return to their homes.
More than 200,000 residents and tourists were forced to flee wildfires in southwest France.
Wildfires have burned over 170 square kilometers in Spain, which is six times more than during the same period in the previous year.
Víctor Resco de Dios, a professor of forestry engineering, stated, "We have entered an era of fires that cannot be extinguished."
Three Greek firefighters died while tackling wildfires on the island of Crete and in the south of the mainland.
The prefecture of Gironde reported that 126 firefighters had been injured since the start of the wildfire in the region.
Across southern Europe, more than 330,000 people were forced to evacuate their homes and hotels due to wildfires.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez stated, "I believe the next 12 hours will be very important," regarding efforts to consolidate wildfire containment near Madrid.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez noted that the national government raised the wildfire near Madrid to "operational level 3" for the first time in Spanish history.
Raging wildfires in southwest France have killed or stranded thousands of wild animals, prompting rescue efforts by firefighters and volunteers.

clusters.headline_hint: Powerful earthquake in Japan kills at least 18 and triggers massive search and rescue operations

claims.text: The Japan Meteorological Agency measured the Kumamoto earthquake on Kyushu island at a magnitude of 7.1, while the US Geological Survey recorded it at 6.8.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated that rescue workers faced a "race against time" to save people trapped in rubble following the earthquake.
Toyota and Honda suspended operations at their factories in Kumamoto until Friday due to ongoing aftershocks and recovery efforts.
An aftershock with an estimated magnitude of 5.8 hit the Amakusa and Ashikita regions of Japan at approximately 10:20 pm.
Kyushu region in southwestern Japan experienced more than 100 aftershocks following the powerful earthquake on Tuesday.
Retail company president Akio Yoshida confirmed that three employees were killed and four were hospitalized after an explosion struck the Aeon Mall in Kashima an hour after the quake.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi deployed more than 4,600 personnel to assist with earthquake search and rescue operations.
Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced on social media that approximately 300 air conditioning units would be flown to Kumamoto to assist evacuees amid high heat.
The quake caused structural damage across Kumamoto prefecture, including the collapse of the worship hall at the 19th-century Yatsushiro Shrine.
TSMC resumed operations at its Kumamoto semiconductor facility on Tuesday evening after passing structural safety inspections following the earthquake.

TSMC established Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing in 2021 with minority investments from Sony Semiconductor Solutions, Denso, and Toyota Motor, planning a combined investment exceeding $20 billion.

clusters.headline_hint: Anthony Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment in tense US Senate hearing on COVID-19 pandemic origins

claims.text: Former US official Dr. Anthony Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment constitutional right to refrain from answering questions during a US Senate Homeland Security Committee hearing on COVID-19 origins.
A group of 155 scientists signed an open letter calling for an end to the harassment of American scientists and stating no credible evidence supported charges against Dr. Anthony Fauci.
Senator Rand Paul announced his intention to hold a committee vote on citing Dr. Anthony Fauci for contempt of Congress.
Former President Joe Biden granted Dr. Anthony Fauci a pre-emptive presidential pardon covering his actions between 2014 and 2025.
In his opening statement, Dr. Anthony Fauci stated that Senator Rand Paul had an "obvious obsession" with prosecuting him to see him "behind bars."
President Donald Trump posted on social media during the hearing, calling Dr. Anthony Fauci "crazy" and accusing him of trying to protect China regarding the origins of COVID-19.

Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul ordered Capitol Police to escort Dr. Anthony Fauci's attorney, David Schertler, out of the hearing room after Schertler spoke without being recognized.
Attorney David Schertler called his removal from the hearing room "outrageous" and accused Senator Rand Paul of conducting a "completely biased and baseless" proceeding.
Responding to Dr. Anthony Fauci's refusal to answer questions, Senator Josh Hawley said during the hearing, "Well, nothing says honesty like taking the Fifth, huh, doc?"
President Donald Trump told reporters regarding Fauci invoking the Fifth Amendment, "Why he did that was very simple: His lawyer told him to."

clusters.headline_hint: Russia files criminal charges against Telegram founder Pavel Durov over alleged espionage and terrorism links

claims.text: Russia's Federal Security Service charged 41-year-old Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism and placed him on an international wanted list.
The FSB alleged that Ukrainian intelligence agencies used a dating chatbot on Telegram to recruit Russian citizens for sabotage and terrorist activities.
Russian authorities reported detaining 46 Telegram users, aged between 12 and 22, over the past year for alleged involvement in arson, attacks on law enforcement, and sabotage.
Following the announcement of criminal charges, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of Pavel Durov displaying an obscene gesture with his middle finger.
Pavel Durov holds dual citizenship in France and the United Arab Emirates and currently resides in Dubai.

Pavel Durov was arrested in Paris in 2024 on preliminary charges related to alleged illicit activities on Telegram, including drug trafficking and child abuse material, before returning to Dubai in March 2025.
Pavel Durov departed Russia in 2014 after declining government demands to close down political opposition groups on his previous social media platform, VKontakte.
Pavel Durov revealed in April 2026 that Russian authorities sent a criminal summons for "Suspect P.V. Durov" to an apartment in Russia where he had not lived for two decades.

clusters.headline_hint: Lok Sabha passes anti-paper leak bill after intense debate over nationwide student protests and NEET probe

claims.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, by voice vote amid opposition protests over police action against student demonstrators.

Under the newly passed bill, individuals convicted of involvement in public exam paper leaks face 5 to 10 years in prison and fines up to Rs 50 lakh, while organized crime carries a minimum 7-year sentence and fines up to Rs 10 crore.
Minister of State Jitendra Singh stated that 52 FIRs have been registered under anti-paper leak legislation since the original law came into effect in 2024.
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following massive student protests over NEET exam paper leaks and irregularities.

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi should leave his position and "become an influencer" following the Prime Minister's social media videos aimed at youth.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke warned that students would launch a larger nationwide protest if the government fails to withdraw criminal FIRs registered against student demonstrators.
Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Ratna Singh disclosed on social media that she has been receiving death threats and abusive messages following the recent student demonstrations.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke returned to his hometown of Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra on July 29 following the conclusion of the 36-day student agitation.

clusters.headline_hint: Meta promises IT Ministry enhanced safeguards for PM Modi's account following video removal dispute

claims.text: Meta sent a formal communication to India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology outlining enhanced oversight measures for content posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other prominent figures.
The controversy arose after Facebook briefly restricted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's July 23 selfie video addressing youth on the NEET paper leak issue due to an automated filtering error.
IT Secretary S Krishnan stated that while Meta apologized for removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's post, the government was "not happy with the explanation" provided and sought additional details.
Meta previously scrapped its "Muse Image" AI feature globally following user privacy concerns over data scraping from public Instagram accounts.
India's IT Ministry summoned Meta's global head of public policy after Facebook briefly took down Prime Minister Narendra Modi's post promising strict action against exam paper leaks.
In his July 23 video address, Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured students that the government would establish fast-track courts and introduce tougher legislation to tackle exam paper leaks.
The Delhi Police Special Cell registered an FIR against social media platform X for allegedly hosting defamatory and malicious posts targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi during student protests.
Delhi Police identified 450 social media accounts that shared alleged deepfakes and AI-generated content during the nationwide youth protests.

clusters.headline_hint: Farmers march on Bhopal over moong MSP as Madhya Pradesh government raises procurement limits

claims.text: The Madhya Pradesh government increased the state's summer moong procurement cap from 25% to 60% of total crop output following protests by nearly 2,000 farmers in Bhopal.
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan reported that Madhya Pradesh had procured approximately 60,000 metric tonnes of summer moong as of July 29, 2026.
State Agriculture Minister Aidal Singh Kansana announced the suspension of the MSP e-token system for fertiliser distribution and extended the moong procurement deadline to August 20.

The Union Government agreed to purchase 4.54 lakh metric tonnes of moong from Madhya Pradesh at a Minimum Support Price of ₹8,780 per quintal, covering about 25% of the state's estimated 20.16 lakh metric tonne output.
Farmers affiliated with Samyukta Kisan Morcha breached police barricades to reach Roshanpura Square in Bhopal, camping within one kilometre of Chief Minister Mohan Yadav's residence.
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav formed a four-member ministerial committee to hold formal negotiations with protesting farmer organizations.
Protesting farmers arrived in Bhopal with tractor-trolleys loaded with five days worth of food and water, vowing not to leave until all their demands were met.
Farmer leaders noted that while the MSP for summer moong was set at ₹8,768 per quintal for the 2026–27 season, excess crop was selling in open markets for only ₹4,000 to ₹5,000 per quintal.

clusters.headline_hint: Crackdown in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir sparks political outrage and Indian diplomatic response

claims.text: More than two dozen people were allegedly killed in firing by Pakistani security forces during violent protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah urged the UN Human Rights Council, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar to intervene in the PoK violence.
The Joint Awami Action Committee, formed in 2003, has been demanding the abolition of 12 seats in the 53-member PoK assembly reserved for refugees from Jammu & Kashmir living in Pakistan.
The Indian Embassy in the United States publicly criticized a New York Times headline, stating that there is no "Pakistani Kashmir," only "Pakistan-occupied Kashmir."
According to local officials and independent estimates cited by The New York Times, at least 30 people died in clashes in PoK between early June and late July.
Pakistani authorities deployed approximately 2,100 army troops and 18,560 police and paramilitary personnel to oversee three-phase elections for 45 directly elected assembly seats in PoK.
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's PoK chapter and the Joint Awami Action Committee boycotted the PoK legislative assembly elections, describing them as a "sham."
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk criticized internet and communications blackouts imposed by Pakistani authorities across parts of PoK during heightened tensions.

clusters.headline_hint: Supreme Court accepts CBI's decision to clear former PM Manmohan Singh in coal block allocation case

claims.text: A Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant accepted the Central Bureau of Investigation's closure report clearing former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in the coal block allocation case.
Former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh passed away in December 2024 while his appeal against a trial court summons remained pending.
In August 2014, the Supreme Court quashed 214 coal block allocations made between 1993 and 2010, declaring them arbitrary and illegal.
Senior Advocates Kapil Sibal and A.M. Singhvi requested the Supreme Court to set aside the trial court's adverse observations against former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh despite his death.
The Supreme Court ruled that the trial court special judge had no valid legal justification for rejecting the CBI's 2014 closure reports that gave Manmohan Singh a clean chit.

clusters.headline_hint: Assam floods death toll rises to 75 as state government steps up relief efforts

claims.text: Seven new fatalities in Sivasagar district raised the death toll from the Assam floods to 75.
The total number of people affected by the floods in Assam dropped to 3.32 lakh across 622 villages and 21 revenue circles.
Charaideo was the worst-affected district in Assam, with 1.42 lakh people impacted by floodwaters.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced that flood-affected families in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat would receive an interim government grant of ₹15,000 for household needs.
Telecom authorities activated Intra Circle Roaming in Sivasagar district to maintain mobile connectivity across all service providers during the flood crisis.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma increased the ex-gratia compensation for families of flood victims from ₹4 lakh to ₹9 lakh, with an additional ₹5 lakh provided from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund.
The Assam state government relaxed compensation rules by eliminating the requirement for a post-mortem report, allowing a certificate from a circle officer to suffice.
More than 45,300 hectares of cropland were submerged by floodwaters across Assam, while the Dhansiri river continued to flow above danger level in Numaligarh district.
